name: Maintain the vehicle fleet
summary: A small in-house garage keeps the utility's roughly 214 vehicles on the road: bucket trucks, digger derricks, cable trucks, trouble trucks and pickups. Work comes from preventive maintenance schedules in the fleet system, defects that drivers find on their daily trip inspection, breakdowns, the annual provincial safety inspection for trucks over 4,500 kg and the annual dielectric test of every insulated boom. The fleet supervisor triages each request by how many people it idles, seven mechanics do the work in eight bays, and outside dealers, body shops and a certified testing firm do what the shop cannot. Delays come from getting a truck released by a busy crew, parts on back order, and outside vendors, and a bucket truck out of service can leave a whole line crew without a vehicle.

baseline.org_archetype: A city-owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 350,000 customers, about 570 staff and about 214 vehicles, maintained by a supervisor and seven heavy-duty mechanics.
baseline.notes: Reference period 2019-2022. Work orders, preventive maintenance schedules, parts and costs are kept in a fleet maintenance system with telematics; parts are ordered through the ERP; drivers complete paper daily inspection reports.

trigger: A preventive maintenance, annual inspection or dielectric test falls due in the fleet system, or a driver reports a defect or breakdown.
end_state: The vehicle is repaired or certified, the work order is closed with labour and parts recorded, and the crew has its vehicle back.

volume.seasonality: Busier in November and December (winter changeovers and storms) and in spring after the winter; dielectric tests and annual inspections are spread through the year by anniversary date.

evidence.note: About 214 vehicles (organisation file resource counts) at two to four preventive services a year, one annual safety inspection for about 85 trucks over 4,500 kg (mto2021), about 70 annual dielectric tests of insulated booms (applus) and about 100 defect and breakdown repairs a month. Agrees with the organisation file's range.

surge.cause: major storm (wind, ice storm, tornado or derecho)

evidence.note: The May 2022 derecho compressed about four years of emergency repairs into 14 days (source); fleet surge frequency and multiplier follow the organisation file's estimate.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Seven heavy-duty mechanics on two weekday shifts; one licensed motor vehicle inspection mechanic or more for annual inspections. The rest of their time is training, shop upkeep and small equipment.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). One supervisor for fleet and facilities; triage, parts ordering, vendors and work order close-out take most of the job, leaving little time for facilities. Many fleets of this size have a fleet coordinator or parts clerk for this desk work.

Organisation file role and cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Not in the process map's roles; releases trucks from crews and arranges drop-off and spares.

systems.name: ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Triage the request and open a work order
steps.description: The fleet supervisor reads the fleet system's due list or the driver's defect report or phone call, opens a work order, and sets its priority by safety and by how many people the vehicle idles; a bucket truck for a four-person crew comes before a pickup.

error.defect_description: Priority set too low for a vehicle that idles a crew.

next.condition: preventive maintenance or annual inspection due
major defect; vehicle out of service

evidence.note: Drivers report defects from the daily inspection and minor defects may be driven until repaired (source); shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take the vehicle out of service and find a spare
steps.description: For a major defect the supervisor tags the vehicle out of service in the fleet system, tells the crew supervisor, and assigns a spare or rental so the crew can keep working.

control.basis: Highway Traffic Act daily inspection rules (Ontario Regulation 199/07): no operation with a major defect

evidence.note: A vehicle with a major defect cannot be operated until repaired (source).

steps.name: Book a bay and a drop-off time
steps.description: The supervisor checks bay and mechanic availability for the shift and agrees a drop-off time with the crew's supervisor, usually after the crew's work day or on a day the crew is in the yard.

steps.name: Crew releases the vehicle
steps.description: The overhead lines supervisor moves the crew to a spare or rearranges work so the truck can go to the garage, and has a crew member drive it in with the keys and the defect report.

steps.name: Drive out to the breakdown
steps.description: A mechanic drives the service truck to the vehicle, diagnoses it at the roadside or work site, and fixes it there when the fault is simple (battery, hose, tire, hydraulic fitting).

steps.name: Towing company brings the truck in
steps.description: A heavy towing company with a unit rated for a loaded bucket truck or digger derrick tows the vehicle to the garage.

steps.name: Check in and diagnose
steps.description: The mechanic pulls the vehicle into a bay, reads fault codes and the telematics history, inspects the reported defect or the preventive checklist items, and lists the parts and labour needed.

error.defect_description: Misdiagnosis leads to the wrong part or repair.

steps.name: Order the parts
steps.description: The supervisor looks up the part with the dealer or parts supplier, raises a purchase requisition or uses a blanket order in the ERP, and records the expected delivery on the work order; the vehicle is parked outside the bay.

steps.name: Wait for parts
steps.description: The supplier ships the parts; common filters and brake parts arrive next day, while boom components, hydraulic cylinders and truck body parts can take weeks.

steps.name: Carry out the service or repair
steps.description: The mechanic performs the preventive service (oil, filters, brakes, lubrication, hydraulic and PTO checks) or the repair, using parts drawn from the shop stock or delivered, and logs readings.

error.defect_description: A fastener, fluid or connection is left incorrect.

steps.name: Perform the annual safety inspection
steps.description: A licensed inspection mechanic inspects brakes, steering, suspension, lights, frame, tires and coupling against the national safety code standard, fixes any failed item, and issues the annual inspection sticker and report.

control.basis: Highway Traffic Act annual inspection of commercial vehicles (Regulation 611) by a licensed inspection mechanic

evidence.note: Trucks over 4,500 kg need an annual inspection valid 12 months, done by a licensed mechanic at an MTO-licensed station (source); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Inspect the aerial device
steps.description: The mechanic inspects the boom, pins, welds, hydraulic hoses and cylinders, controls, fall-arrest anchors and outrigger interlocks of the bucket or digger derrick against the manufacturer's checklist and the aerial device standard, and operates it through its full range.

control.basis: Periodic inspection of vehicle-mounted aerial devices under CSA C225 and the manufacturer's manual

evidence.note: CSA C225 covers inspection and maintenance of vehicle-mounted aerial devices (source); interval and time are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Road test and check the work
steps.description: The mechanic road tests the vehicle or runs the equipment, checks for leaks and warning lights, and confirms the defect is fixed before releasing it.

steps.name: Record labour, parts and readings
steps.description: The mechanic enters labour hours, parts used, odometer and engine hours, and what was found and done in the fleet system work order, which resets the next preventive maintenance date.

error.defect_description: Hours or parts missing, or odometer not updated so the next service is mistimed.

steps.name: Send the vehicle to an outside vendor
steps.description: For warranty, body, transmission, upfitter or boom structural work the supervisor gets a quote, raises a purchase order and arranges transport to the dealer or specialist shop.

steps.name: Vendor repairs the vehicle
steps.description: The dealer or specialist shop schedules, repairs and returns the vehicle with an invoice; warranty claims and back-ordered parts can stretch this to weeks.

steps.name: Book the dielectric test
steps.description: The supervisor books the boom's annual dielectric test with a certified testing firm on a date when a spare can cover the crew, and arranges to take the truck to the tester's facility or have the mobile unit come.

evidence.note: Annual testing at the tester's facility or by mobile unit (source); lead time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Testing firm runs the dielectric test
steps.description: The testing firm applies high voltage across the insulating boom sections, liners and extensions, measures leakage current against the acceptance limits and issues a certificate or a failure report.
outputs: dielectric test certificate or failure report

control.basis: Annual dielectric test of insulating aerial devices (CSA C225 as required by provincial occupational health and safety rules)

next.condition: fails; boom or liner repair needed

evidence.note: Annual dielectric testing required for aerial devices and digger derricks in Canada under CSA C225 (source); pass rate and duration are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the vendor's work and invoice
steps.description: The supervisor inspects the returned vehicle, compares the vendor invoice with the quote and purchase order, and approves it for payment.

control.basis: Receipt and invoice approval within delegated authority

steps.name: File the test certificate
steps.description: The supervisor scans the dielectric certificate into the vehicle file, updates the test date in the fleet system and places a copy in the truck as crews and auditors expect.

steps.name: Close the work order and return the vehicle
steps.description: The supervisor reviews the completed work order for labour, parts and readings, closes it so costs post to the vehicle, and tells the crew supervisor the vehicle is ready.

control.basis: Fleet records kept for each vehicle as the operator's maintenance record

exceptions.name: Parts on back order
exceptions.description: The vehicle waits outside the bay for parts ordered through the ERP.

exceptions.name: Breakdown in the field
exceptions.description: A mechanic drives out; half are fixed on site and half are towed in.

exceptions.name: Failed dielectric test
exceptions.description: The boom fails its test and goes to a specialist shop before it can be used near energized lines.

benchmarks.population: Aerial devices and digger derricks in Canada

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from work order opened to vehicle returned

evidence.note: Scheduled services wait a few days for a bay and a release from the crew; parts and vendor work stretch the tail. Not measured.

pain_points.description: Trucks are hard to get released from crews, so preventive services slip and turn into breakdowns.
Back-ordered parts and outside vendors keep vehicles out of service for weeks, idling crews or forcing rentals.
Labour and odometer readings are typed in after the job and are sometimes missing, which mistimes the next service.

sources.title: Commercial vehicle safety requirements (archived 2021-08-28)
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Transportation, via Library and Archives Canada web archive
sources.supports: Trucks over 4,500 kg need an annual inspection valid for 12 months, done by a licensed motor vehicle inspection mechanic at an MTO-licensed inspection station; drivers do a daily inspection within 24 hours before driving and report defects to the operator; a vehicle with a major defect cannot be operated; the operator repairs defects immediately or before the next dispatch and keeps repair records.

sources.title: Dielectric testing of aerial devices and digger derricks
sources.supports: Dielectric testing is required annually for all aerial devices and digger derricks operating in Canada under provincially mandated standards including CSA C225; the insulating booms, extensions, bucket and liners are tested indoors at the tester's facility, with mobile testing available.

sources.title: The Trees Are Winning: Hydro Ottawa Is Using Remote Sensing to Fight Back (A. Kemp)
sources.supports: Before the 2022 pilot Hydro Ottawa trimmed on fixed cycles under OEB direction, rural circuits every three years and urban circuits every two; planning relied on ground patrols and outage history; contractor work was verified with small field samples; the May 2022 derecho put more than 180,000 customers out and compressed about four years of emergency repairs into 14 days.

assumptions: Fleet size of about 214 vehicles is the sum of the organisation file's resource counts (42 bucket trucks, 14 digger derricks, 16 cable trucks, 12 trouble trucks and 130 light vehicles); no opened source gives the utility's fleet size.

The garage is assumed to be an MTO-licensed inspection station with at least one licensed inspection mechanic, so annual inspections are done in-house; dielectric tests are contracted to a certified testing firm.
Preventive maintenance orders are generated by the fleet system itself; this is shown as a trigger from this process because the organisation file has no separate fleet planning process.
Defect reports come from every field process that drives trucks, not only overhead construction and outage restoration as the process map lists.
Triage shares, repair times, parts lead times and vendor turnaround are the author's estimates.
